newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk board chairman thinks strike won't happen.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk board chairman thinks strike won't happen.

text.p: The Norilsk Nickel metal group's board chairman, Vsevolod Generalov, said on Friday he did not think workers at Norilsk's flagship plant would strike, and management was working to resolve the issue.
"I hope there will be no strike -- I don't think there will be one," Generalov told Reuters before a metallurgy conference.
He said Norilsk management was reviewing the time over which it would repay salary arrears, adding, "I think we'll find a solution. The situation is getting better."
Union leaders at Norilsk's flagship plant, the Norilsk mining and metallurgical complex, plan strikes on March 27 and April 2 over wage and vacation arrears.
Norilsk owes flagship plant workers around 900 billion roubles in wages unpaid over two months and about 1.2 trillion roubles to various budgets.
Generalov said RAO Norilsky Nickel, the parent company of the flagship plant, was in talks with regional budget officials on a repayment schedule.
"I think we'll reach some sort of consensus," he said.

He also said Norilsk was seeking government permission to export its own precious metals output, including palladium and platinum. All exports are now done through the state agency Almazjuvelirexport.

A statement from Uneximbank, which holds a 38 percent stake, or 51 percent of voting shares, in the Norilsk group and is restructuring the company, said it was considering a $300 million programme to resettle Norilsk pensioners to less expensive regions.
There are about 44,000 pensioners in the town of Norilsk out of a total of 300,000 residents. Uneximbank said it would finance the resettlement with its own and domestic finances.
Norilsk has said that social costs are killing its revenues. Norilsk spent 4.5 trillion roubles, or around 40 percent of its revenues, in 1996 on social costs in its main town.
